question: How does the analogy of pot-space illustrate apparent division within space?
premises: A pot creates an apparent division in space
The space inside the pot is called pot-space
This division is due to the limiting adjunct, not to space itself
inference: Just as pot-space appears divided by the pot, reality may appear divided by limiting conditions.
uncertainties: The verse is syntactically incomplete and continues into the next verse
plain_english: Just as, by the division of the potter's wheel, pot-space appears in the pot.
